requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to provide NAT so node2 and node3 processes can reach the internet through it
requirements.summary: node1 (VyOS) configured with eth1=10.50.50.254/24 and a source NAT masquerade rule (rule 100, source 10.50.50.0/24 -> outbound eth0), committed and saved. node2/node3 configured with static IPs (10.50.50.11/.12) on ens7 and a low-metric default route via node1. Ping and curl from node2/node3 succeeded over ens7, and conntrack on node1 directly showed live translation of 10.50.50.11/.12 traffic to node1's WAN IP (10.100.62.10), confirming NAT is functioning end-to-end.

requirements.requirement: NAT and network configuration should be durable (not just runtime state)
requirements.summary: NAT rule was committed and saved (VyOS 'save') rather than left as an uncommitted runtime change, and node2/node3 interface configs were written to persistent /etc/network/interfaces.d files rather than only applied with ephemeral 'ip' commands. Post-reboot checks confirm the configuration survived a full restart.

overall_summary: The core task — NAT egress from node2/node3 through node1 — is directly and convincingly demonstrated: committed VyOS masquerade rule, static private-network addressing on both Ubuntu nodes, and successful ping/curl plus conntrack translation evidence. The mandated node-restart protocol was also executed correctly for all three nodes, with pre-restart boot IDs, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and confirmed recovery of NAT configuration and connectivity afterward. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified in the command trace.
limitations: A few intermediate VyOS diagnostic commands failed due to shell/session issues (e.g., 'run' or 'configure'/'show' not found outside an active vbash config session), but these were read-only diagnostic attempts superseded by correctly-formed follow-up commands that succeeded, so they do not affect the outcome assessment.
Internet reachability was verified via ICMP/HTTP to 1.1.1.1 and example.com rather than a broad set of destinations, but this is a reasonable and standard proxy for general internet egress.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands in order: node1 interface/NAT configuration (cmd-20b3c325286444b7) and its commit/save were necessary and directly tied to the task outcome; node2/node3 static IP and route configuration (cmd-e45ce19496644120, cmd-7e878935959e4baa) were necessary prerequisites for egress; the three sequential reboots (cmd-1062ab611b8949a7, cmd-f90c5a44c2d0457e, cmd-07ceba50b665496e) were performed to satisfy the mandated node-restart evidence protocol, one node at a time, with health verified after each. No unnecessary, unrelated, destructive, or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were found; a few diagnostic commands failed harmlessly due to shell/command-not-found issues (e.g. cmd-d1e170105c264d5e, cmd-e9f868eddb6f4527) but did not mutate state and were followed by corrected read-only retries. Post-reboot temp file/socket differences reflect normal OS boot churn, not executor-caused residue.
